title: Prevent chronic hepatitis C infection with a licensed vaccine

concept.text: Prevent establishment of chronic HCV infection after exposure, including in people at continuing risk of reinfection. A 548-participant randomized vaccine trial induced immune responses but failed to prevent chronic infection. Proposed completion test: Regulatory licensure following a randomized field efficacy trial showing significantly fewer incident chronic HCV infections than control, using a prespecified persistent-infection endpoint and at least 12 months of exposure follow-up. Test set by: A regulator would decide licensure. The NIAID-funded trial defined chronic infection as persistent viraemia for six months; the follow-up minimum here is editorial. Overlaps: VIR-04. Sources given: [Randomized HCV vaccine trial](https://www.nejm.org/doi/pdf/10.1056/NEJMoa2023345?articleTools=true) ; [WHO hepatitis C factsheet](https://www.who.int/news-room/fact-sheets/detail/hepatitis-c).

page.title: Licensed prophylactic hepatitis C vaccine
page.definition: A preventive vaccine licensed for a specified population would reduce the risk that exposure to hepatitis C virus (HCV) results in chronic infection. A vaccinated person could still acquire HCV and clear it. The human efficacy trial defined chronic infection as persistence of viral RNA in blood for six months.

goal.need: About 47 million people live with chronic hepatitis C, and roughly 900,000 new HCV infections occur each year. Of those with chronic infection, 15–30% develop cirrhosis within 20 years. Antivirals can cure more than 95% of people with hepatitis C, but access to testing and treatment is limited, and people can acquire HCV again after cure. Vaccination before exposure could spare people chronic liver disease and the need for treatment. Its impact depends on reaching people at risk, including people who inject drugs.

completion.title: FDA licenses a vaccine with an indication covering prevention of chronic hepatitis C infection.
completion.criterion: FDA issues a biologics licence for a preventive HCV vaccine, with an approved indication covering prevention of chronic HCV infection in a specified population. FDA determines that the clinical evidence establishes safety and effectiveness, that benefits outweigh risks for that population, and that manufacturing and facility information establish product quality and consistency.
completion.set_by: U.S. Food and Drug Administration, 21 CFR 601.4 and Vaccine Development – 101; these are general vaccine licensure requirements.
completion.threshold_quote: the establishment(s) and the product meet the applicable requirements established in this chapter.
completion.basis: Licensure supplies an external decision covering clinical benefit, safety and manufacturing. FDA bases the approved indication on satisfactory supporting data. WHO reports that no effective HCV vaccine exists. No HCV-specific minimum efficacy percentage or protection duration was identified in the regulatory sources searched.

milestones.title: An HCV vaccine enters human testing under an investigational new drug application in effect.
milestones.criterion: The sponsor submits preclinical safety data and information on vaccine quality and manufacture to FDA. A human study begins with the investigational new drug application in effect. The application takes effect 30 days after FDA receives it unless FDA imposes a clinical hold, or earlier if FDA notifies the sponsor that the study may begin.
milestones.set_by: U.S. Food and Drug Administration, 21 CFR 312.40(a)–(b).
milestones.threshold_quote: Thirty days after FDA receives the IND, unless FDA notifies the sponsor that the investigations described in the IND are subject to a clinical hold

milestones.title: The HCV vaccine trial clears its interim safety and immune-response review for stage 2.
milestones.criterion: In NCT01436357, the monitoring board reviews blinded data from both arms after stage 1 (planned enrolment 68 ± 4). The rule for proceeding is no safety concern and an HCV-specific response in at least 30% of evaluable participants across both arms. Evaluation requires a sample 7–21 days after dose two. A response after either dose, before infection, counts if any of six peptide pools yields more than 48 spot-forming cells per million peripheral blood mononuclear cells and at least three times mean background. Missing the threshold triggers independent unblinded review.
milestones.set_by: NIAID Division of Microbiology and Infectious Diseases, protocol 10-0069, section 11.3, registered as NCT01436357.
milestones.threshold_quote: at least 30% of the evaluable subjects in Stage 1 of the study (n = 68 ± 4) have a positive immune response to HCV.

milestones.title: An HCV vaccine significantly reduces six-month persistent infection in a randomized field trial.
milestones.criterion: In HCV-uninfected adults aged 18–45 who injected drugs in the preceding 90 days, the vaccine group has a lower hazard of six-month chronic HCV infection than the placebo group in the per-protocol analysis (two-sided stratified log-rank test, α = 0.05). The analysis stratifies by sex and IFNL3 genotype. Persistence requires the same virus at initial detection and 159–201 days after incident infection, confirmed by sequence comparison, plus an intervening RNA-positive sample. If several samples fall in the window, use the one closest to day 180.
milestones.set_by: NIAID Division of Microbiology and Infectious Diseases, NCT01436357 protocol and statistical analysis plan, sections 3.3 and 8.1 of the plan.
milestones.threshold_quote: Treatment groups will be tested at the 2-sided 5% significance level.

milestones.title: An HCV vaccine completes phase 3 studies and FDA files its licence application.
milestones.criterion: Phase 3 studies supply effectiveness and safety evidence, and commercial manufacturing development supports consistent production. FDA receives the complete Biologics License Application, including nonclinical and clinical results, manufacturing methods, stability data and proposed labelling, and considers it filed for review. FDA describes successful clinical development and a reproducible manufacturing process as preceding this submission.
milestones.set_by: FDA, vaccine development pathway and filing requirements in 21 CFR 601.2(a); these requirements concern biological products generally.
milestones.threshold_quote: An application for a biologics license shall not be considered as filed until all pertinent information and data have been received

milestones.title: An HCV vaccine candidate elicits an HCV-specific immune response in an animal model.
milestones.criterion: Immunization with the candidate produces a measurable HCV-specific antibody or cellular response in an appropriate animal model. The study measures the response to the vaccine antigens.
milestones.set_by: World Health Organization, WHO Technical Report Series 927, Annex 1, section 3, guidance on nonclinical immunogenicity.
milestones.threshold_quote: Nonclinical immunogenicity studies should assess the relevant immune response, e.g. humoral and/or cell-mediated immune response, induced in the vaccinated animals.

milestones.title: Controlled phase 3 studies show protection against chronic HCV infection and characterize safety.
milestones.criterion: In the intended population, phase 3 studies compare chronic HCV infection in vaccine recipients and controls and demonstrate effectiveness on the prespecified clinical endpoint. Safety follow-up in the larger study population characterizes adverse events, including less common events.
milestones.set_by: U.S. Food and Drug Administration, Vaccine Development – 101, phase 3 clinical development.
milestones.threshold_quote: critical information on effectiveness and additional important safety data

milestones.title: FDA files the biologics licence application for a preventive HCV vaccine.
milestones.criterion: FDA receives all pertinent information and data and considers the application filed. The submission includes nonclinical and clinical evidence, manufacturing methods and sites, product stability data, representative samples and lot-test summaries, and proposed labelling.
milestones.set_by: U.S. Food and Drug Administration, 21 CFR 601.2(a).
milestones.threshold_quote: An application for a biologics license shall not be considered as filed until all pertinent information and data have been received

not_found: Searches of WHO preferred-product-characteristic resources and FDA guidance found no HCV-specific minimum vaccine efficacy or required protection duration for licensure.
No published efficacy threshold specifically requiring protection against reinfection after HCV cure was found.

results.finding: In 9 evaluated ChAd3-NSmut/MVA-NSmut recipients, all 9 developed HCV-specific T-cell responses.
results.detail: The phase 1 study enrolled 15 volunteers and reported no serious adverse reactions. It says an efficacy study had started, but does not report a safety review recommending progression to phase 2.
results.quote:
HCV-specific T cell responses were significantly enhanced by MVA-
NSmut boost in all volunteers, peaking 1 week after vaccination (median,
2355; range, 1490 to 6117 SFCs/106 PBMCs; peak after ChAd3-NSmut
prime versus peak after MVA-NSmut boost;P = 0.0039; Fig. 1, A and B).

results.finding: The phase 1 HCV vaccine study at Oxford enrolled 15 healthy volunteers.
results.detail: The paper also reports that NCT01436357 had started in the United States, with no details on FDA receipt of an IND, the 30-day period, a clinical hold, or earlier FDA notification.
results.quote:
A totalof 24 volunteers were assessed for
eligibility, and 15 volunteers were enrolled in one of two arms.

Reason: The definition leaves unclear whether a transient infection after vaccination is compatible with protection against chronic hepatitis C.
